text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will strike a deal in August with the State Ownership Fund (FPS) to purchase a majority stake in Romania's Arctic Gaesti refrigerator maker.
- The FPS will put 17 companies on flotation on the Bucharest bourse starting September.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Petrobrazi oil refinery, based in the oil city of Ploiesti, announced it would cut by 10 percent prices of oil products starting August.
- Shares in stainless steel maker Otelinox will be traded on the Bucharest bourse starting July 31.
- The FPS has put 1,200 companies in private hands this year, the fund's president Sorin Dimitriu said. He said the FPS signed privatisation contracts worth $230 million with 130 foreign investors.
ADEVARUL
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea pledged to speed up liquidation of loss-making state-run companies, during a meeting with Romania's largest trade union confederations.

- The government is expected to announce budget revision figures on Thursday, amid efforts to cut budget spending to most ministries and increase allocations for health, education and social security.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- According to a draft project for the privatisation of Romania's flag carrier Tarom, the company will offer 49 percent to foreign investors, while the control stake would be held by Romanian investors, transport ministry Secretary of State Marian Francu said.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The government prefect in the central city of Cluj has filed a complaint to the prosecutor's office, saying mayor Gheorghe Funar incited the population to illegal and hostile actions against the Hungarian consulate.
- The newspaper runs a full-page report on floods and "devastating rainfall" in the past four days which have inundated hundreds of houses throughout the country.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said the government was considering financial aid for flooded areas.
ADEVARUL
- Road transport trade unions will parade through central Bucharest on Wednesday with trucks and vans in a protest against a road tax due to be introduced in August.
- Eight miners in the Jiu Valley coal mining area were badly injured by an explosion triggered by a gas leak in the Vulcan mine.
- More than 300 families in the western Banat region, near the border with Serbia, were left homeless by floods, the newspaper says.
- Trade unions demanded salary indexation and wage tax cuts during a meeting with the government.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu sacked police spokesman Nicolae Bucur, following a press statement released by Bucur criticising the country's medical staff for "widespread corruption" and saying the police would hunt down corrupt doctors.

- Many ethnic Hungarians want their children to study in Romanian-language schools, despite recent amendments to the education law allowing ethnic minorities to secure tuition in their mother tongue at any level across Romania. ($ = 7,240 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
